rows.title: Along Colorado’s I-70 detour route, speeding, traffic jams — and an occasional boost to business
rows.standfirst: Between late June and late August, I-70 through Glenwood Canyon closed nine times as state officials prepared for flash floods or cleared the roadway after car and truck accidents.

rows.standfirst: Eagle County is the only Colorado group appealing the Surface Transportation Board’s approval of a new Utah railroad that will direct 350,000 barrels of Uinta Basin crude through Colorado.

rows.title: COVID homeless hotels are closing from Denver to Anchorage, sending some back to streets
rows.standfirst: Cities from Anchorage to New Orleans have ended or are winding down their hotel programs, which offered a good alternative to packed homeless shelters amid the spread of COVID-19

rows.title: The sudden suspension of a Colorado prison-work program has thrown employers into disarray
rows.standfirst: The Take Two program was paused following an inmate escape earlier this year. Employers, already battling a tight labor market, say they were given no time to plan for the loss of labor.

rows.standfirst: A diverse group of entrepreneurs talk about the difficulties of being a startup trying to attract attention and funding.

rows.title: Colorado legislature faces inflationary budget crunch as risk of recession grows

rows.title: State budget writers fear consequences of Colorado voters approving affordable housing ballot measure

rows.title: These Colorado programs are helping beginning farmers overcome huge challenges
rows.standfirst: The programs are especially critical given that farmers in the U.S. are aging faster than young farmers are getting in line to take their place. One-third of the 3.4 million American farmers are over the age of 65, according to latest Census of Agriculture.

rows.title: A quarter of Colorado’s 981 orphan wells went dormant when one natural gas gathering system was shut down
rows.standfirst: Adams County was especially hard when Third Creek pipelines were dismantled because of safety concerns. Small operators walked away from 225 wells.

rows.title: Buena Vista residents had to pay $166 to get mail. Now, the USPS says it will deliver for free.
